newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Daimler sells Gemini stake, sees earnings push. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Daimler sells Gemini stake, sees earnings push. [CORRECTED 15:45 GMT]

text.p: German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG said on Thursday it had ended its six-year relationship with French software maker Cap Gemini in a deal that would have a substantial impact on 1997 earnings.

Klaus Mangold, chief executive of Daimler services unit Debis, said Cap Gemini's holding company CGIP had agreed to buy the German group's 24.4 percent stake in Gemini for 1.4 billion marks ($793.9 million) in cash.
(Corrects to make clear CGIP and not Cap Gemini bought shares from Germany's Daimler)

"CGIP accepted our share offer last evening. We will have round about 1.4 billion marks in cash," Mangold told reporters during a meeting of central and eastern European political and business leaders in this Alpine city.
He added the transaction would be closed by July 28.
"This will have a very big impact on our earnings, and of course on the group's earnings as well," a Debis spokesman told Reuters. He declined to be more specific.

Debis said it would cancel a recently launched convertible bond issue to sell the Gemini shares and would pay holders of the notes 104 percent (Corrects from four percent) of their original investment in cash.
The notes were to have a maturity of four-and-half years and to be exchanged into Gemini shares at the option of investors.
"We will pull off the issue since CGIP had the first right of refusal (on the shares). We have foreseen this as one of the scenarios," Mangold said.
Mangold added Daimler would use some of the proceeds of the sale to strengthen its position in the emerging markets of central and eastern Europe.

"Daimler-Benz will step up its joint-venture activities in the region," he said. "I see an enormous potential for growth in Daimler-Benz activities in the region - despite all obstacles, risks and problems."
Mangold said Daimler's 1996 turnover in the region rose 18 percent to 1.3 billion marks and that sales were already up by at least the same amount since the start of this year.
Daimler signalled last month it would pull out of Cap Gemini because of differing strategic focuses and because U.S. regulations hindered Cap Gemini's business there.
The U.S. Bank Holding Company Act put a lid on Cap Gemini's business in the States because Deutsche Bank AG holds a stake in Daimler.
In a statement, Daimler also said Cap Gemini would return its 19.6 percent stake in Debis unit Debis Systemhaus.
Debis originally invested 1.1 billion marks in Cap Gemini in 1991, and later made a 170 million mark capital injection.

Its disposal of the stake came just three months after Mangold was quoted as saying the Daimler unit may increase its Gemini holding to a majority stake to help it exploit growing international demand for information technology.

Daimler last month said Debis had developed a different strategic focus to that of Cap Gemini, targeting capital intensive business and outsourcing while the French company was primarily active in the software market.
